issues.failure_explanation: The proof of Theorem thm:main:mgdl obtains the residual decay by re-applying Theorem thm:main:mgdl:one:op to each block residual. That theorem realizes its updates as h_k = A_k^out ∘ (ReLU∘A_k) ∘ ⋯ ∘ (ReLU∘A_1) with maps constructed for the current target starting from the raw input (Stage I). The proof of thm:main:mgdl then relabels the second application's maps as A_{n_1+1},…,A_{n_1+n_2} and writes the updates as A_k^out ∘ ocomp_{i=1}^k(ReLU∘A_i), i.e. chained through the frozen first-stage maps, and concludes R_k = f_{k+1} 'by construction'. No compatibility argument is given showing the second-stage cutoffs (whose geometry is defined on the input domain) can be computed through the frozen first-stage chain, whose action on the input is a fixed nonlinear map; the chained term is a different function from the analyzed update. The gap persists under either reading of the composition order (the paper's literal definition ocomp_{i=1}^n f_i = f_1∘⋯∘f_n is also the reverse of the order used in the construction, compounding the mismatch). Hence the identity R_k = f_{k+1} for the Φ_k displayed in the theorem is never established.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert a passthrough/compatibility lemma: each grade's affine map carries d scaled copies of the input coordinates (within aff_{≤5d}) so newly added blocks can realize their cutoffs through the frozen chain, state it as part of Theorem thm:main:mgdl:one:op, and correct the ocomp ordering; then the iterative assembly and R_k = f_{k+1} follow. Or restate the theorem's architecture as the stage-wise concatenation actually produced by the argument.
issues.overall_effect: The main theorem's construction and its conclusions (i)-(ii) are not established by the written proof; the corollary and the paper's headline prose claims (first rigorous guarantee of grade-wise vanishing error) lose their support.
issues.title: Re-applied one-step updates are not realizable inside the frozen multigrade chain; R_k = f_{k+1} is not established
issues.why_classification: A complete repair needs a contained but genuine realizability argument (passthrough invariant plus width verification plus an ordering fix); no new global proof architecture is required and every substantive guarantee (rates, strict monotone decay, uniform vanishing) survives, so this is more than minor but short of serious.

issues.failure_explanation: The explicit Γ_Q is the arithmetic mean of one-dimensional trapezoids, Γ_Q(x) = (1/d)Σ_j ψ(2(x_j−c_j)/ℓ), not a product-type combination: ψ(u_j) = 0 only kills the j-th summand, so Γ_Q(x) can be as large as (d−1)/d at points where a single coordinate leaves the slab, i.e. far outside rQ, contradicting the defining property Γ_Q = 0 off rQ. Concrete counterexample (d=2, r=3/2): let g be a smooth ridge near the line [0,1]×{δ/2} so that E_{g,ε} meets every grid cube Q_{(i,0)} = [iδ,(i+1)δ]×[0,δ], i = 0,…,K−1. At x = (δ/2, δ/2) we have Γ_{Q_{(0,0)}}(x) = 1, while for each i ≥ 1, Γ_{Q_{(i,0)}}(x) = ½[ψ(−2i) + ψ(0)] = ½, since |2(x_1−c_1)/ℓ| = 2i ≥ 2 > r yet the x_1-term of ψ is the only vanishing one. Hence Σ_i Γ_{Q_{(i,0)}}(x) = 1 + (K−1)/2 → ∞ and T_ε g(x) = ε M_g Σ_i Γ_i is unbounded, violating condition C1 (0 ≤ T_ε g ≤ g⁺ ≤ M_g). The proof of Lemma lem:T:positive:eps:contraction fails exactly at its two uses of the false support property — the overlap estimate Σ_i Γ_{Q_{g,ε,i}}(x) ≤ 2^d via Lemma lem:bounded:overlap:scaling and the claim T_ε g(x) = 0 outside ⋃_i rQ_{g,ε,i} — so T_ε satisfies neither C1 nor the pointwise bounds used in Stage II, and the symmetrized operator S_ε inherits the failure.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the aggregation in Definition def:dilated-cube-cutoff by a clamped (minimum-type) combination, e.g. Γ_Q(x) = σ(Σ_{j=1}^d ψ(2(x_j−c_j(Q))/ℓ(Q)) − (d−1)) with σ = ReLU; this equals 1 on Q, lies in [0,1], and vanishes identically off rQ, so every estimate in Lemma lem:T:positive:eps:contraction and downstream goes through verbatim. The network realization then needs one additional clamping ReLU per cutoff (e.g. the paper's own two-affine-map grade blocks, or width 5d+1); adjust the architecture claims accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: T_ε is not a positive ε-contraction, Lemma lem:positive:to:balanced:eps:contraction cannot be applied to it, so S_ε is not established as a balanced contraction; Theorem thm:main:mgdl:one:op (uniform accuracy, pointwise domination, strict L^p monotonicity), the proof of Theorem thm:main:mgdl, and Corollary coro:mgdl:residual all collapse, and the advertised guarantee of grade-wise vanishing residual error loses its support.
issues.title: Constructed cutoff functions do not vanish off the dilated cube, so the overlap bound fails and T_ε is not a positive ε-contraction
issues.why_classification: The repair is a localized modification of one construction (one extra clamping ReLU, or a two-affine-map grade block as the paper itself uses experimentally); with it, the three defining cutoff properties hold trivially, all estimates in the lemmas and both main theorems go through unchanged, and no advertised rate, regime, or conclusion is lost — a contained, nontrivial but non-architectural fix, hence moderate rather than minor, and far short of serious.
